title: Latent dynamics for reconstructing fine-scale PDE trajectories from coarse observations
abstract: arXiv:2610.33722v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Coarse PDE observations omit spatial detail and intermediate states of evolving fields. We present Structured Latent Dynamics (SLD), a framework that reconstructs high-resolution trajectories from spatially and temporally downsampled simulations. SLD interpolates the input in time, adds a learned temporal correction and uses the resulting sequence to guide a hidden state on the coarse grid. Each update of the latent state combines a learned gated response with horizontal and vertical central differences and a five-point Laplacian of the state. The three spatial terms have learned channel-wise coefficients. Two Haar wavelet synthesis branches map the hidden state and refined coarse input to the high-resolution field. We evaluate SLD on two-dimensional Gray--Scott, complex Ginzburg--Landau and viscous Burgers systems, reconstructing 100 output frames from 25 input frames with eightfold refinement in each spatial direction. translated_title: 用于从粗粒度观测重建细尺度PDE轨迹的潜在动力学方法
translated_abstract: 粗粒度的PDE观测缺失了演化场的空间细节和中间状态。我们提出了结构化潜在动力学（Structured Latent Dynamics, SLD），这是一个从空间和时间上降采样的模拟数据中重建高分辨率轨迹的框架。SLD对输入进行时间插值，加入一个可学习的时间校正，并利用所得序列来引导粗网格上的隐藏状态。潜在状态的每次更新将可学习的门控响应与状态的水平、垂直中心差分以及五点拉普拉斯算子相结合。这三个空间项均具有可学习的通道级系数。两个Haar小波合成分支将隐藏状态和精细化后的粗输入映射到高分辨率场。我们在二维Gray–Scott、复Ginzburg–Landau和粘性Burgers系统上评估SLD，从25个输入帧重建100个输出帧，并在每个空间方向上实现八倍细化。SLD实现了较低的
tldr: 提出结构化潜在动力学（SLD）框架，通过结合可学习门控响应与有限差分、拉普拉斯空间算子的潜在状态更新机制，以及Haar小波合成分支，从时空降采样的粗粒度PDE观测中重建高分辨率演化轨迹，在Gray–Scott、Ginzburg–Landau和Burgers系统上实现了从25帧到100帧、空间八倍细化的重建。
en_tdlr: Structured Latent Dynamics (SLD) reconstructs high-resolution PDE trajectories from spatiotemporally downsampled coarse observations by combining learned gated responses with finite-difference and Laplacian spatial operators in latent state updates, using Haar wavelet synthesis branches for upsampling, achieving 100-frame reconstruction from 25 input frames with eightfold spatial refinement on Gray–Scott, Ginzburg–Landau, and Burgers systems.
